authority: Delegated user SPEC only: exact compiled bytes, explicit HOST adapters, lifecycle/cleanup, configured public-build semantics, safe actual HTTPS payload, independent canonical/collector readback. Not a general product review.

findings.requirement: Endpoint/key must not be echoed by comparison failures or compiled/adapter exceptions.
findings.defect: assert.equal retains and formats actual/expected endpoint and write_key. Assertion errors escape the try/finally or asynchronous timer callback unsanitized. Descriptive assertion messages do not hide values.
findings.verified: Executed the exact realHTTPS function only with sentinel strings and an in-memory transport. Both URL and key mismatch AssertionError stacks contained expected and actual sentinel values. No real secrets were read.
findings.fix_boundary: Boolean comparisons with fixed safe codes, and sanitized top-level/asynchronous error reporting; never serialize AssertionError actual/expected or raw compiled exceptions.

findings.requirement: Response/error completion must be exactly once; late failures and outstanding request resources must be closed before final evidence.
findings.defect: done is set only by req.error, never by res.end. Success then late request error invokes both options.success and options.fail; record.ack stays true. IncomingMessage error/aborted have no handlers. Requests/sockets are not tracked or cancelled by finalization; clearing QA timers cannot quiesce HTTPS callbacks.
findings.verified: Exact realHTTPS function with EventEmitter request/response: success_callbacks=1, fail_callbacks_after_success=1, response_error_listener_count=0, response_aborted_listener_count=0. No sockets or SDK bundle used.
findings.fix_boundary: Single settled completion gate shared by all response/request outcomes, response error/aborted handling, bounded transport teardown, and failure state captured before immutable report generation.

findings.requirement: Failure report and cleanup must survive onDestroy exceptions; original failure must remain identifiable without secret text.
findings.defect: Unguarded app.onDestroy in finally precedes timer cleanup and report write. If it throws, it replaces the original error and skips both cleanup and evidence. Extraction/config/init failures before line 75 likewise have no safe report path.
findings.verified: Executed exact finalizer with only stubs: original PRIMARY_SENTINEL was replaced by DESTROY_SENTINEL, cleanup_calls=0, report_writes_to_stub=0, live_timers_after=1.
findings.fix_boundary: Preserve safe primary failure code, catch destroy failure separately, perform cleanup in nested finally, and write passed=false evidence even when initialization or destruction fails.

findings.requirement: onDestroy/clean must be verified, not simulated by harness cleanup.
findings.defect: passed=true is decided before destruction. Finalizer then forcibly clears all timers and reports remaining_timers=0 regardless of whether product onDestroy leaked timers. module_status is the pre-destroy snapshot; stopped pending/busy and restored console are not asserted.
findings.verified: Exact finalizer with a destructor that leaves one timer: cleanup_calls=1, reported_passed=true and reported_remaining_timers=0. This is QA-finalizer verification only, not a claim the actual product leaks.
findings.fix_boundary: Capture and assert post-destroy state and adapter resource counts before emergency cleanup; only mark success afterward. Report pre-cleanup leakage separately.

findings.requirement: public-build placeholder config has a key, therefore expect configured; public means truly disabled configuration only.
findings.defect: Example labels /actual/public.app as --expect public and instructs the parent to run those two commands. For the stated placeholder public-build APP that is the wrong expected state; false failure or misleading public coverage follows. The script's expected_configuration_matches logic itself is correct.
findings.fix_boundary: Document public-build APP with --expect configured; reserve --expect public for independently identified genuinely disabled compiled input. Do not use raw source as compiled input.

non_blocking_scope_notes: HOST script converts exact input bytes to UTF-8 and verifies byte roundtrip, uses explicit ViewModel/requireNative/timer adapters, observes original logger closure via inspector, verifies configured and disabled lifecycle separately, and suppresses raw execution error text. No additional static HOST-script SPEC defect established in this scope; not an actual compiled-APP pass.

HOST report app_js_sha256 is independently checkable for --js. For --app it records archive entry names and JS digest but not enclosing APP/HAP digests; parent must bind extraction to the specific new CI APP. new_ci_provenance_verified=false is honest and must remain false until independent provenance verification.

HTTPS reports actual supplied APP and compiled JS SHA256 and captures generated requests, but ACK is transport/application acknowledgement only. Canonical cloud and independent collector exact marker/stage readback remain separate mandatory parent work.

HTTPS method reads actual APP bytes without source/export rewrite; the adapter-only probes used QA functions with in-memory stubs, not synthesized SDK output. No new SDK/APP was manufactured, extracted or executed during this review.
README's prior CI/current-evidence assertions were not revalidated; old products, old reviews and green gates were deliberately outside scope.
disposition: BLOCKED. Parent should fix the scoped QA/README defects and run targeted adapter failure/cleanup tests before exercising the actual new configured CI APP. This report is not native/WE/CI success and must not replace independent canonical/collector readback.
